title: Repo-scoped install mode and machine-binary delegation
description: WHY: teams need bwrk scoped to the repo - version pinned in the lockfile, nothing on the machine PATH - and the machine binary must not fight the pinned version, because two bwrk versions writing one .boreal state is how schema-drifted records happen. WHAT: (1) make the published package work as a dev dependency: node_modules/.bin/bwrk points at the bundled entrypoint from the dist-build task, pnpm bwrk and npx bwrk work in a repo with no machine binary, and the package exposes whatever bin metadata that requires; (2) delegation - when the machine-installed binary starts inside a workspace whose project has a repo-pinned bwrk (detect node_modules/.bin/bwrk relative to the discovered workspace root, or an explicit pin recorded in project config), it re-executes the pinned binary with identical argv and environment and exits with its exit code; delegation happens before any state read or lock acquisition so the machine version never touches pinned-repo state; recursion guard via env var so the pinned binary never re-delegates; a no-delegate flag skips for debugging; (3) bwrk version output reports both identities when delegating (launcher version and channel, then delegated version); (4) record the pin in the project registry entry when a linked repo has one, so the global dashboard can surface skew later. Tests: delegation round-trip with two built versions in fixture dirs, recursion guard, no-delegate flag, and a no-pin repo running the machine binary directly.
acceptanceCriteria: pnpm bwrk works in a fixture repo with no machine binary, covered by a test
Machine binary inside a pinned repo re-executes the pinned version before any state access, with recursion guard and the no-delegate flag covered by tests
Version output shows both identities when delegating
closedReason: completed repo-scoped install and delegation task
